claims.quote: New open standards created in the mobile era, such as HTML5, will win on mobile devices (and PCs too).
claims.claim: Open web standards such as HTML5, rather than Adobe Flash, will prevail on mobile devices and on PCs.
claims.resolutionCriteria: Flash is abandoned as the main platform for rich web content on mobile browsers and on desktop browsers, replaced by HTML5 and related open standards.

source.title: Thoughts on Flash (open letter on apple.com, archived copy)

grading.rationale: Adobe stopped developing mobile-browser Flash in November 2011, YouTube made HTML5 its default desktop player in January 2015, and in July 2017 Adobe announced Flash's end of life, citing matured open standards such as HTML5.

evidence.title: Adobe Discontinues Development of Flash Player on Mobile Devices
evidence.snippet: Our future work with Flash on mobile devices will be focused on enabling Flash developers to package native apps with Adobe AIR for all the major app stores.

evidence.title: YouTube Now Streams HTML5 Video By Default
evidence.snippet: Starting today, YouTube defaults to using HTML5 video on all modern browsers, including Chrome, IE 11, Safari 8 and the beta versions of Firefox.

evidence.title: Flash & the Future of Interactive Content
